outcome: The conjecture remains open for n >= 3 (proved for n = 1, 2 since 1965); the only claimed advance against it — Bryant and Ferry's announced counterexamples for every n >= 6, first presented at the March 2018 Spring Topology Conference — has still not been published or posted to arXiv as of September 2026, and continues to be cited by working topologists as unpublished. No new mathematical result, published or preprint, moving the conjecture itself has appeared since 26 January 2024.
summary: The triage record correctly identified the only candidate event in this space: J. Bryant and S. Ferry's March 2018 announcement, at the Spring Topology Conference, of counterexamples to the Bing-Borsuk conjecture for every n >= 6 (infinitely many topologically distinct homogeneous ANR-compacta of dimension n, n >= 6, that are not topological manifolds). That announcement predates the frozen revision by nearly six years, so even if it were published it would be open_stale rather than a within-window event. But the more important finding is that it still has not been published anywhere, in any version, as of this research (September 2026). I checked: (1) Valov's 'Homogeneous metric ANR-compacta' (arXiv 2003.06907, March 2020) cites the Bryant-Ferry result as an unpublished announcement; (2) Valov's 'Homogeneous locally compact spaces' (arXiv 2401.00341, posted 2 January 2024, i.e. right before the frozen revision) again cites it as unpublished, with no arXiv identifier or journal reference for a Bryant-Ferry paper — a web-search summary in the triage record claimed this paper referenced a 'revised version' of the counterexample paper, but on actually opening and reading the PDF I found no such revised-version claim; it treats the result as it always has, an unpublished announcement; (3) Valov's newest paper on this cluster, 'Homology manifolds and homogeneous compacta' (arXiv 2505.07196, submitted 12 May 2025 — within the window), does not even discuss the Bing-Borsuk conjecture or the Bryant-Ferry counterexamples; it proves an unrelated characterization of almost-homology n-manifolds among homogeneous ANR-spaces, so it is not a case or a variant of this problem, just adjacent literature; (4) I could not locate a Bryant-Ferry preprint under any plausible title on arXiv directly. The Wikipedia article itself (English, current live version, opened for orientation only per the rules) still states the conjecture is proved only for dimensions 1 and 2 and mentions no counterexample at all — it appears not to have been updated even to reflect the 2018 announcement, let alone anything from the window. In short: no event in the 26 January 2024 to present window changes what a careful reader would write in this bullet. The pre-window 2018 announcement, were it ever published, would be classified open_stale, but since it has still not appeared in any citable form even by 2026, there is nothing to date and no status change to record; 'open' is the honest classification, and I record no_change_found rather than open_stale because there is no publication event to stamp a date on, only a standing unpublished announcement whose status is unchanged since before the frozen revision. No AI system appears anywhere in this literature; all authors are working topologists (Valov, Bryant, Ferry) doing conventional point-set/geometric topology.
competing_reading: One could argue for open_stale on the theory that the 2018 Bryant-Ferry announcement effectively settles the general conjecture (for n>=6) and that its non-publication is a technicality of academic norms rather than a live mathematical uncertainty, in which case the 'true' resolution predates the frozen revision and the record should be open_stale with the 2018 date noted. I rejected this because the rules for resolved/claimed require either expert digestion of a written argument or a manuscript at all, and here there is no manuscript to digest — an announced-but-never-written-up result is weaker than even a 'claimed' status, and every secondary source I found (2020, 2024, and implicitly 2025) continues to describe the conjecture as open precisely because the counterexample was never published. Treating an unwritten announcement as settling anything would overstate what happened.
what_would_settle_it: The actual appearance of a Bryant-Ferry (or successor) manuscript — on arXiv, in a journal, or as a citable preprint with a specific identifier — giving the construction of the n>=6 counterexamples, together with any expert digestion of it (e.g., a review, a citation that engages with its proof rather than merely citing the announcement). Absent that, the question is settled only for n=1,2 and remains genuinely open for n=3,4,5 and unpublished/unconfirmed for n>=6.

dead_ends: The Jonathan Heindl thesis PDF fetch returned corrupted/unreadable text via WebFetch; could not confirm its date or content directly, though search snippets suggest it is a general survey rather than a source of new results.

No arXiv identifier for any Bryant-Ferry counterexample paper could be found under any searched title; it appears never to have been posted to arXiv at all, consistent with every secondary source calling it unpublished.

The triage's found item at arxiv.org/pdf/2401.00341 was suspected (via a search-engine summary) to reference a 'revised version' of the Bryant-Ferry paper; on actually opening and reading the PDF, no such claim was present — this appears to have been a hallucinated or misattributed search summary, and I could not verify it.
